note.text:
How to recognise each fireplace in a drawing:
• Three-stone fireplace: three stones on the ground, the fire between them, the pot resting on the stones.
• Improved (mud) stove: a solid block of mud or clay with a small door in front for the firewood and a hole on top for the pot.
• Charcoal stove: a small metal stove, often on legs, with black pieces of charcoal glowing red under the pot.
When you draw a fireplace, label the pot, the fire, the fuel (wood or charcoal) and what holds the pot.

worked_example.problem: Which fireplace in the drawing is the charcoal stove?
steps: Look for a small metal stove on legs, with black charcoal under the pot.

cards.idea: A three-stone fireplace shows three stones on the ground with the fire between them.
example: The pot rests on the three stones.

cards.idea: An improved stove is a solid block of mud or clay with a door in front for wood.
example: Only a little of the fire can be seen, through the door.

cards.idea: A charcoal stove is a small metal stove, often on legs, with glowing charcoal under the pot.
example: Charcoal is black; it glows red when it burns.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: In a drawing, a three-stone fireplace shows three stones on the ground.
An improved stove has a door in front for firewood.
A charcoal stove is often made of metal.

wrong.text: A charcoal stove is drawn as three stones.
wrong.explain: Three stones show the three-stone fireplace; a charcoal stove is a metal stove.

wrong.text: An improved stove has no walls.
wrong.explain: An improved stove has mud or clay walls.

wrong.text: A three-stone fireplace burns charcoal in a metal box.
wrong.explain: A three-stone fireplace burns firewood between three stones.
